free_tier.stated: Up to 1,000 uploaded files per Google account (2 GB max per file per the Partner Center spec; the consumer uploader historically enforced 100 MB). 1,000 x 2 GB ≈ 2 TB theoretical per Google account.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: No egress metering for reading, but there is no public direct-download URL: files are served through the authenticated Play Books reader. Not CDN-cacheable, not shareable as a link.

tooling: Web upload only (play.google.com/books -> Upload files). No public API; third-party tools are downloaders for purchased books, not uploaders.
chaining: 1,000 files x 2 GB = ~2 TB per free Google account, x unlimited free Google accounts. This is the Drive-service-account pattern applied to Play Books; it is only blocked by the absence of an upload API.
limits_note: 1,000-file cap per account; 2 GB/file (Partner Center) vs 100 MB in the consumer uploader; EPUB/PDF only; uploads are re-processed into Google's internal format, so the stored artifact is not byte-identical to what you sent.
